description: SmartRoadSense is a crowdsensing system that estimates road surface roughness from the accelerometer and GPS of smartphones carried in vehicles. The open data provide CSV points about every 20 m along roads, each with a PPE roughness index, the OpenStreetMap way identifier and highway class and the time of the last update. Aggregated values are updated every six hours, and a weekly history is kept. Coverage is wherever app users drive, mostly in Italy. Access: free CSV downloads from the project website under the Open Database License, credited as "© SmartRoadSense contributors". Caveats: coverage depends on volunteer trips, the index is relative, not a standard IRI measurement, and quiet roads have few readings. It supports road condition and deterioration analysis, maintenance prioritisation and inputs to road network vulnerability studies, and complements national road databases such as the Norwegian NVDB catalogued here.
name: SmartRoadSense crowdsensed road surface roughness
